title: Self-Discovery Cycle
opening: A lesson can be saved and still miss the next attempt. The Self-Discovery Cycle carries an experience into a useful change while keeping its original conditions and observations available.

labels.cycleIntro: Move through the four actions. The detail panel shows what each action asks you to do.
labels.practiceIntro: Use an actual attempt or event. Keep observation, interpretation and uncertainty distinct. Saving a note alone does not integrate the learning.
labels.exampleNotice: Illustrative example loaded; it is not an observed outcome.
labels.length: Shorten the full note to fit the 2,000-character limit. Your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote: Use the Self-Discovery Cycle: Experience → Capture → Reflect → Integrate. Capture the event and conditions, reflect on what the account explains, and integrate the useful change into the next attempt. Keep the original observation or source behind a summary.
labels.private: This note is private and optional; six required course questions remain separate.

feedback.unavailable: Private saving is unavailable. Your note stays on screen.
feedback.length: Shorten the full note to fit the 2,000-character limit. Your text stays here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved version before saving again.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.

steps.title: Experience
steps.detail: Start with an event or attempt that could inform later action.

steps.title: Capture
steps.detail: Record what happened and the relevant conditions. Preserve the original observation or source.

steps.title: Reflect
steps.detail: Separate the observation from the interpretation. Name what the account explains and what remains uncertain.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.detail: Place a useful change in the next attempt, tool, instruction, or arrangement so later work can use it.

fields.label: What event or attempt are you learning from?
What happened, and under which conditions?
Where can you return to the original observation or source?
What does the account explain, and what remains uncertain?
What useful change will the next attempt, tool, or arrangement inherit?

example.event: A learner misunderstands one instruction in a lesson.
example.conditions: The misunderstanding appears when the example changes from paper to software; the exact learner wording is retained.
example.source: Keep the learner’s original question beside the lesson section it concerns.
example.reflection: The example may hide a step. It is not yet clear whether the wording or the sequence caused the confusion.
example.next: Revise that example in the lesson learners use, then check a later independent attempt.

source.assessmentBoundary: Six required open-ended course questions remain separate from optional private practice. No qualified semantic grade or learner outcome is supplied.
